## Interfaces checked

- MP Definition 4.3.1 and the surrounding properties define the psh cone as
  a decreasing model completion and give rational/real translation stability.
  MP Theorem 4.3.8 is the divisorial comparison principle.  The finite-energy
  ray interface is in MP Theorems 5.1.4 and 5.1.7 and Section 5.2.
- Xia Section 4 works in the compact Kähler setting.  Its Lemma 4.2 gives
  divisorial order reflection; Definition 4.7 and Corollary 4.8 give maxima;
  Definition 4.9 and Lemma 4.10 give decreasing infima with their endpoint
  and divisorial formulas.  Section 3.2 and Lemma 3.10 give positive-volume
  recovery by an unperturbed curve.
- DXZ Definition 3.3, formula (43), and Theorem 3.17 supply the inverse
  system, normalized finite-energy formula, and finite-energy ray
  correspondence.
- The P14.2 all-point upper-semicontinuity theorem and the dominated
  divisorial-density theorem are already live, independently audited Chapter
  71 inputs.  They are hypotheses/dependencies here, not silently reproved.

The compactness/directedness proof of MP decreasing stability and the full
truncation deduction are new arguments, not claims attributed verbatim to a
source.

## Boundary checks

The proof uses no metrizability or countable cofinality of the model category:
each `phi_j` is resolved by a net, and only the explicit truncation parameter
`j` is sequential.  The continuous minimum in the stability proof is not
declared psh.  Finite energy is obtained only after zero-tail and
positive-volume recovery.  No uniform lower energy bound in `j` is needed.

The trivial semivaluation is included when endpoints are compared.  The
all-point equality is not inferred from ordinary density: it uses the
dominated divisorial net, upper semicontinuity, ideal antitonicity, and the MP
comparison principle.

The conclusion is conditional on P14.2, is restricted to Kähler classes, and
does not assert an unchanged MP theory for big non-nef or zero-volume classes.

# P14.3 full Kähler truncation closure — production statement

Let `X` be a connected compact Kähler manifold, let `alpha=[omega]` be a
Kähler class, and let `K=X^beth` be the compact space of semivaluations of
coherent ideal sheaves.  Assume the all-point P14.2 conclusion: the literal
raw ideal-valuative transform of every DXZ non-Archimedean psh object is upper
semicontinuous on `K`.

The following previously established interfaces are part of the statement's
context.

1. The MP cone `PSH_MP(alpha)` is the decreasing-net completion of rational
   PL model psh functions.  Rational translations preserve the model cone.
2. Rational divisorial semivaluations, including the trivial semivaluation,
   approximate every semivaluation from below in ideal order.  Consequently,
   an upper-semicontinuous ideal-antitone function that agrees divisorially
   with an MP psh function agrees with it everywhere.
3. DXZ objects admit maxima with constant objects and decreasing infima when
   their endpoints have a finite lower bound.  On rational divisorial points,
   the raw transform sends a maximum to the pointwise maximum and a decreasing
   infimum to the pointwise infimum; at the trivial semivaluation it equals
   the endpoint.  Divisorial raw-transform values determine the DXZ object
   and reflect order.
4. In a Kähler class, positive-volume DXZ objects are recovered by
   unperturbed positive-mass test curves.  The finite-energy DXZ--MP
   correspondence is bijective and preserves energy; the literal raw
   transform of a finite-energy object equals its MP image at every
   semivaluation.
5. The constant DXZ object of value `a` has test-curve level zero below `a`
   in every Kähler perturbation component.  Every normalized model level is
   at most zero.
6. The previously verified MP-section theorem constructs a unique map
   `S_alpha:PSH_MP(alpha)->PSH_DXZ^NA(X,omega)` on the full MP cone, without
   a finite-energy restriction, and proves
   `T_alpha(S_alpha(phi))=phi` at every semivaluation.  This section preserves
   and reflects pointwise order.

## Decreasing-stability lemma

If `(phi_j)_{j>=1}` is a decreasing sequence in `PSH_MP(alpha)` and
`phi=inf_j phi_j` is not identically minus infinity, then
`phi in PSH_MP(alpha)`.

## Kähler truncation theorem

Under the preceding hypotheses, the literal raw ideal-valuative transform is
an order isomorphism

`T_alpha: PSH_DXZ^NA(X,omega) -> PSH_MP(alpha)`.

Its inverse is the previously constructed MP-to-DXZ section.  More precisely,
for a DXZ object `Gamma`, let `0` be the constant zero object and put

`Gamma^(j) = Gamma vee (0-j)`.

Then every `Gamma^(j)` has finite energy,
`Gamma^(j) downarrow Gamma`, and

`T_Gamma = inf_j T_{Gamma^(j)}`

on all of `K`, with every function on the right in `E^1_MP(alpha)`.  On the
finite-energy locus this order isomorphism is the existing finite-energy
DXZ--MP correspondence and the energies agree.

## Scope

The theorem is conditional only in the explicit sense above: it uses the
all-point P14.2 upper-semicontinuity conclusion.  It removes the independent
P14.3 residual in Kähler classes without projectivity, rationality, or a
finite-energy hypothesis.  It does not extend the relatively nef MP cone
unchanged to a big non-nef class and does not construct an unnormalized
energy or Monge--Ampère operator in a zero-volume class.

P14.3 FULL KÄHLER TRUNCATION CLOSURE — PRODUCTION PROOF

1. Decreasing stability of the MP cone

Let H=PL(K) intersect PSH_MP(alpha). For every j, choose a decreasing
model net h_(j,lambda) downarrow phi_j in H. Let S consist of all h in H
such that h >= phi_j + epsilon for some j>=1 and some positive rational
epsilon. Rational translation shows that S is nonempty.

We prove that S is downward directed. Suppose
h_i >= phi_(j_i)+epsilon_i for i=1,2. Choose j>=max(j_1,j_2) and a
positive rational delta with 4 delta < min(epsilon_1,epsilon_2). For the
continuous comparison function g=min(h_1,h_2), one has
phi_j+4 delta<g everywhere on compact K. The open sets

{h_(j,lambda)+2 delta<g}

form a directed increasing cover of K. Compactness first gives a finite
subcover, and directedness of the approximating net then gives one index
lambda for which the displayed inequality holds on all of K. Therefore
h=h_(j,lambda)+delta belongs to S and satisfies h<=h_1,h_2. The minimum g
was used only as a continuous comparison function; no closure of the psh
cone under minima is assumed.

Order S by reverse pointwise order. Its identity net is a decreasing net
in H. Every member dominates phi=inf_j phi_j, so the net's infimum is at
least phi. Conversely, fix x in K and a real b>phi(x). Choose j with
phi_j(x)<b, and then choose a positive rational epsilon and an index lambda
such that h_(j,lambda)(x)+epsilon<b. The function
h_(j,lambda)+epsilon belongs to S and is smaller than b at x. Thus
inf_(h in S) h=phi pointwise, including where phi=-infinity. Since the
limit is not identically minus infinity, the defining MP decreasing-net
completion gives phi in PSH_MP(alpha).

2. Finite-energy truncations

Fix a DXZ object Gamma, write c=Gamma_max, and set c_j=max(c,-j). In every
Kähler perturbation class omega+eta, the constant object of value -j has
level zero for tau<-j. The maximum Gamma^(j)=Gamma vee (0-j) dominates
that object, while each normalized model level is at most zero. Hence

(Gamma^(j),omega+eta)_tau=0 for tau<-j.

Its minus-infinity level therefore has full mass in every perturbation
component, so its DXZ volume equals V_alpha=int_X omega^n>0.
Positive-volume recovery supplies an unperturbed positive-mass test curve
gamma^(j) in the class omega. The levelwise recovery formula preserves the
zero tail, so gamma^(j)_tau=0 for tau<-j. Consequently

E^0(gamma^(j)) = c_j V_alpha
                 + int_(-j)^(c_j)(M_omega(gamma^(j)_tau)-V_alpha) d tau

lies in [-j V_alpha,c_j V_alpha], because the integrand lies in
[-V_alpha,0]. Thus Gamma^(j) has finite energy. This proves finite energy
from the actual zero tail of the recovered curve, not from a merely
divisorial lower bound.

3. Recovery of the original DXZ object

Maximum is monotone, so Gamma^(j) decreases with j. Its endpoints are
c_j downarrow c, and hence the decreasing DXZ infimum exists. At every
positive rational divisorial point q, the maximum and infimum formulas give

T_(inf_j Gamma^(j))(q)
= inf_j max(T_Gamma(q),-j)
= T_Gamma(q).

The endpoint formula gives the same equality at the trivial semivaluation.
Divisorial injectivity therefore yields inf_j Gamma^(j)=Gamma.

4. Positivity of the literal raw transform

Let phi_j in E^1_MP(alpha) correspond to Gamma^(j) under the finite-energy
bijection. The established all-point finite-energy comparison gives
phi_j=T_(Gamma^(j)) on all of K. The sequence is decreasing by monotonicity
of the raw transform. At the trivial semivaluation,

inf_j phi_j(0)=inf_j c_j=c> -infinity,

so phi=inf_j phi_j is not identically minus infinity. Section 1 gives
phi in PSH_MP(alpha). The divisorial maximum formula and the endpoint
formula give phi=T_Gamma on the entire rational divisorial locus.

By the assumed P14.2 conclusion, T_Gamma is upper semicontinuous. It is
antitone for ideal order directly from its multiplier-ideal formula. The
dominated divisorial comparison interface therefore promotes the divisorial
equality to phi=T_Gamma at every semivaluation. This proves both the
asserted pointwise truncation formula and that the literal raw transform
maps the entire DXZ cone into the MP cone.

5. Isomorphism, order, and energy

Established interface 6 supplies the previously constructed section S_alpha
and the identity T_alpha o S_alpha=id on the full MP cone. Since the raw
transform is divisorially injective,
S_alpha o T_alpha=id on the DXZ cone. Pointwise monotonicity of the raw
transform and divisorial order reflection show that both maps preserve and
reflect order. On the finite-energy locus, divisorial identification and
injectivity identify this map with the existing finite-energy DXZ--MP
correspondence, so its energy identity applies. This completes the proof.
